claim: DIAPH3 localizes at the centrosome during prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase of mitosis.
source: (A–D) Immunostaining of U2OS cells at prophase (A), metaphase (B), anaphase (C), and telophase (D), with anti-DIAPH3 (green) and anti-γ tubulin (magenta). The chromosomes were counterstained with DAPI (blue). Diaphanous three (DIAPH3) localizes at the centrosome at all mitotic stages.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showing co-localization of DIAPH3 with centrosomal marker γ-tubulin across all mitotic stages, supported by microscopy images in Figure 1A-D.

claim: DIAPH3 signal is pericentrosomal during mitosis.
source: Insets are zooms in the centrosomal region, showing that the DIAPH3 signal is pericentrosomal.
evidence: High magnification insets in Figure 1A-D demonstrate the pericentrosomal localization pattern of DIAPH3.

claim: DIAPH3 localizes at the midbody during telophase.
source: In telophase, it was also seen at the midbody (Figure 1D), which is consistent with its documented role in the ingression of the cleavage furrow during cytokinesis (Watanabe et al., 2013; DeWard and Alberts, 2009).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showing DIAPH3 at the midbody during telophase, consistent with prior published studies on its role in cytokinesis.

claim: shRNA against DIAPH3 significantly reduces DIAPH3 protein levels in U2OS cells.
source: shRNA against DIAPH3 (sh-DIAPH3) significantly reduced the levels of DIAPH3 and SPAG5 proteins (p=0.000044 and 0.000046, respectively).
evidence: Western blot analysis with quantification showing statistically significant reduction in DIAPH3 protein levels upon shRNA knockdown (Figure 1E,F).

claim: shRNA against DIAPH3 significantly reduces SPAG5 protein levels in U2OS cells.
source: shRNA against DIAPH3 (sh-DIAPH3) significantly reduced the levels of DIAPH3 and SPAG5 proteins (p=0.000044 and 0.000046, respectively).
evidence: Western blot analysis with quantification showing statistically significant reduction in SPAG5 protein levels upon DIAPH3 knockdown (Figure 1E,F).

claim: shRNA against SPAG5 reduces SPAG5 and DIAPH3 protein levels in U2OS cells.
source: Reciprocally, shRNA against SPAG5 (sh-SPAG5) reduced SPAG5 and DIAPH3 protein levels (p=0.000001 and 0.000097, respectively).
evidence: Western blot analysis with quantification showing statistically significant reduction in both SPAG5 and DIAPH3 protein levels upon SPAG5 knockdown (Figure 1E,F).

claim: 82% of DIAPH3 knockdown cells exhibit mitotic abnormalities compared to 4% in control cells.
source: 82% of DIAPH3 knockdown cells exhibit mitotic abnormalities (4% in control cells). n = 118 and 115 cells from five individual experiments of scrambled shRNA and sh-DIAPH3, respectively.
evidence: Quantification of mitotic errors from immunofluorescence analysis of 118 control and 115 DIAPH3 knockdown cells across five experiments (Figure 1K).

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown causes lagging chromosomes during mitosis.
source: Yellow arrows in (H) point to lagging chromosomes.
evidence: Microscopy images showing lagging chromosomes in DIAPH3 knockdown cells (Figure 1H).

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown causes multipolar spindles.
source: Arrowheads in (I) depict poles of mitotic spindle.
evidence: Microscopy images showing multiple spindle poles in DIAPH3 knockdown cells (Figure 1I).

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown causes disorganized/shrunk microtubules, single centrosome/pole, and asymmetric metaphase plate.
source: (J) Representative image of a mitotic cell with disorganized/shrunk microtubule (MT), single centrosome/pole, and asymmetric metaphase plate.
evidence: Microscopy image showing multiple mitotic defects in DIAPH3 knockdown cells (Figure 1J).

claim: 40% of DIAPH3 knockdown cells exhibit an abnormal number of centrosomes.
source: Notably, DIAPH3 knockdown compromised the integrity of the centrosome and bipolar shape of the spindle (40% of cells exhibited an abnormal number of centrosomes), as well as the organization of MT, leading to mis-segregation of chromosomes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Quantification data from immunofluorescence analysis showing centrosome abnormalities in DIAPH3 knockdown cells.

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown reduces cortical actin by 48% in mitotic cells.
source: (N) Quantification of cortical actin (fluorescence intensity) showing a reduction of 48% of cortical actin in DIAPH3 knockdown cells. n = 113 cells per condition from three distinct experiments. Student's t-test, p=1.07 × 10−32.
evidence: Quantitative fluorescence intensity measurements of phalloidin-stained cortical actin in 113 cells per condition across three experiments (Figure 1L-N).

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown reduces cell survival to 59.1 ± 0.73% of control cells.
source: Knockdown of DIAPH3 also reduced cell survival to 59.1 ± 0.73% of control cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), likely by inducing apoptosis (percentage of aCas3+ cells: 1.1 ± 0.12% for scrambled shRNA versus 3.2 ± 0.16% for Diaph3 shRNA; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Cell counting data from three independent experiments showing reduced survival in DIAPH3 knockdown cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown increases apoptosis from 1.1 ± 0.12% to 3.2 ± 0.16% of cells.
source: likely by inducing apoptosis (percentage of aCas3+ cells: 1.1 ± 0.12% for scrambled shRNA versus 3.2 ± 0.16% for Diaph3 shRNA; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Quantification of activated caspase-3 positive cells from immunofluorescence analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: DIAPH3 knockdown does not affect cell proliferation as measured by Ki67+ cell ratio.
source: However, it did not affect cell proliferation as the ratio of Ki67+ cells was preserved (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Quantification of Ki67+ cells showing no significant difference between control and DIAPH3 knockdown conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).

claim: GPSM2 protein levels are downregulated in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: In contrast, polarity proteins GPSM2, NUMB, and PAR3, and microtubule-associated proteins SPAG5 and KNSTRN were downregulated (Figure 2A,B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing reduced GPSM2 levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: NUMB protein levels are downregulated in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: In contrast, polarity proteins GPSM2, NUMB, and PAR3, and microtubule-associated proteins SPAG5 and KNSTRN were downregulated (Figure 2A,B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing reduced NUMB levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: PAR3 protein levels are downregulated in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: In contrast, polarity proteins GPSM2, NUMB, and PAR3, and microtubule-associated proteins SPAG5 and KNSTRN were downregulated (Figure 2A,B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing reduced PAR3 levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: SPAG5 protein levels are downregulated in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: In contrast, polarity proteins GPSM2, NUMB, and PAR3, and microtubule-associated proteins SPAG5 and KNSTRN were downregulated (Figure 2A,B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing reduced SPAG5 levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: KNSTRN protein levels are downregulated in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: In contrast, polarity proteins GPSM2, NUMB, and PAR3, and microtubule-associated proteins SPAG5 and KNSTRN were downregulated (Figure 2A,B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing reduced KNSTRN levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: NUMA protein levels are not significantly changed in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: We did not detect significant changes in the level of endogenous NUMA, dynein, dynactin, INSC, or CLASP1 between Diaph3 cKO and control mice.
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing no significant change in NUMA levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: Dynein protein levels are not significantly changed in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: We did not detect significant changes in the level of endogenous NUMA, dynein, dynactin, INSC, or CLASP1 between Diaph3 cKO and control mice.
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing no significant change in dynein levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: Dynactin protein levels are not significantly changed in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: We did not detect significant changes in the level of endogenous NUMA, dynein, dynactin, INSC, or CLASP1 between Diaph3 cKO and control mice.
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing no significant change in dynactin levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: INSC protein levels are not significantly changed in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: We did not detect significant changes in the level of endogenous NUMA, dynein, dynactin, INSC, or CLASP1 between Diaph3 cKO and control mice.
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing no significant change in INSC levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: CLASP1 protein levels are not significantly changed in Diaph3 cKO telencephalon.
source: We did not detect significant changes in the level of endogenous NUMA, dynein, dynactin, INSC, or CLASP1 between Diaph3 cKO and control mice.
evidence: Western blot analysis of telencephalon lysates from Diaph3 cKO mice showing no significant change in CLASP1 levels (Figure 2A,B).

claim: SPAG5 localizes to the spindle pole and kinetochore during metaphase in control cells.
source: In control cells, the protein localized to the spindle pole and kinetochore during metaphase and progressively concentrated in the pericentrosomal region as mitosis proceeded to anaphase (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: Immunofluorescence images showing SPAG5 localization pattern in control cells during metaphase (Figure 2C,D).

claim: SPAG5 progressively concentrates in the pericentrosomal region as mitosis proceeds to anaphase in control cells.
source: In control cells, the protein localized to the spindle pole and kinetochore during metaphase and progressively concentrated in the pericentrosomal region as mitosis proceeded to anaphase (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: Immunofluorescence images showing SPAG5 localization pattern in control cells during anaphase (Figure 2C,D).

claim: SPAG5 expression and distribution are disrupted in DIAPH3-depleted cells.
source: In DIAPH3-depleted cells, SPAG5 expression declined sharply (Figure 1E,F; Figure 2C–H), and its distribution was disrupted (Figure 2E–H, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Western blot and immunofluorescence data showing reduced SPAG5 levels and altered localization in DIAPH3 knockdown cells (Figures 1E,F and 2C-H).

claim: Spag5 mRNA expression pattern resembles that of Diaph3 with strong expression in cortical progenitor cells.
source: Importantly, the expression pattern of the Spag5 transcript resembled that of Diaph3 with a strong expression in cortical progenitor cells (http://www.eurexpress.org/ee/databases/assay.jsp?assayID=euxassay_004999&image=01; Damiani et al., 2016).
evidence: Expression data from the Eurexpress database and previous publication showing similar expression patterns of Spag5 and Diaph3 in cortical progenitors.

claim: Spag5 mRNA is reduced by 78% in Diaph3 cKO compared to control mice.
source: (I) Quantification of the Spag5 mRNA by real-time RT-PCR. There is a reduction of 78% in Diaph3 cKO relative to control mice (p=0.0046). n = 3 from nine embryos for each genotype.
evidence: Real-time RT-PCR quantification from nine embryos per genotype showing statistically significant reduction in Spag5 mRNA (Figure 2I).

claim: Spag5 mRNA expression is downregulated in Diaph3 cKO as shown by RNAscope in situ hybridization.
source: (J) Coronal sections of e11.5 forebrain from control (left) and Diaph3 cKO (right, hybridized with a Spag5 fast red-labelled RNAscope probe). The expression of Spag5 mRNA is downregulated in Diaph3 cKO; scale bar, 150 µm. n = 3 for each genotype.
evidence: RNAscope in situ hybridization images from three embryos per genotype showing reduced Spag5 mRNA in Diaph3 cKO (Figure 2J).

claim: Silencing SPAG5 in U2OS cells triggers multipolar spindles and chromosome mis-segregation.
source: Silencing SPAG5 in U2OS cells triggered multipolar spindles and chromosome mis-segregation, a phenotype reminiscent of DIAPH3 knockdown (Figure 1G–J and Figure 3A–D; Thein et al., 2007).
evidence: Immunofluorescence images showing mitotic defects in SPAG5 knockdown cells similar to DIAPH3 knockdown (Figures 1G-J and 3A-D), consistent with published literature.

claim: SPAG5 knockdown compromises the expression and/or stability of DIAPH3.
source: It also compromised the expression and/or stability of DIAPH3 (Figure 1E,F and Figure 3A–D).
evidence: Western blot and immunofluorescence data showing reduced DIAPH3 levels in SPAG5 knockdown cells (Figures 1E,F and 3A-D).

claim: Overexpression of SPAG5 significantly rescues cell viability in DIAPH3 knockdown cells from 59.1 ± 0.73% to 87.1 ± 1.71%.
source: Remarkably, overexpression of SPAG5 significantly rescued the DIAPH3 knockdown phenotype and partially restored cell viability (survival: 87.1 ± 1.71% in SPAG5 rescue versus 59.1 ± 0.73% in DIAPH3 knockdown; aCas3+ cells: 1.1 ± 0.15% in SPAG5 rescue versus 3.2 ± 0.16% in DIAPH3 knockdown; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B) and spindle bipolarity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Cell survival assays showing rescue of DIAPH3 knockdown phenotype by SPAG5 overexpression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).

claim: Overexpression of SPAG5 reduces apoptosis in DIAPH3 knockdown cells from 3.2 ± 0.16% to 1.1 ± 0.15%.
source: Remarkably, overexpression of SPAG5 significantly rescued the DIAPH3 knockdown phenotype and partially restored cell viability (survival: 87.1 ± 1.71% in SPAG5 rescue versus 59.1 ± 0.73% in DIAPH3 knockdown; aCas3+ cells: 1.1 ± 0.15% in SPAG5 rescue versus 3.2 ± 0.16% in DIAPH3 knockdown; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B) and spindle bipolarity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Apoptosis assays showing rescue of DIAPH3 knockdown phenotype by SPAG5 overexpression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Overexpression of SPAG5 partially restores spindle bipolarity in DIAPH3 knockdown cells.
source: Remarkably, overexpression of SPAG5 significantly rescued the DIAPH3 knockdown phenotype and partially restored cell viability (survival: 87.1 ± 1.71% in SPAG5 rescue versus 59.1 ± 0.73% in DIAPH3 knockdown; aCas3+ cells: 1.1 ± 0.15% in SPAG5 rescue versus 3.2 ± 0.16% in DIAPH3 knockdown; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B) and spindle bipolarity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Immunofluorescence images showing rescue of spindle bipolarity by SPAG5 overexpression in DIAPH3 knockdown cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).

claim: shRNA against SPAG5 reduces SPAG5 protein levels by 82.8% in NIH3T3 cells.
source: (E, F) Western blot analysis of SPAG5 levels upon shRNA-mediated downregulation in NIH3T3 cells. Transfection of shRNA against SPAG5 (sh-SPAG5) significantly reduced the protein levels (−82.8%, p=0.00001, n = 3 independent experiments, Student's t-test; error bars represent s.e.m.).
evidence: Western blot quantification from three independent experiments showing statistically significant reduction in SPAG5 protein levels (Figure 3E,F).

claim: 49% of SPAG5 knockdown cells undergo non-planar divisions compared to 31% in control cells in vivo.
source: 49% (67/137) of SPAG5 knockdown cells underwent non-planar divisions versus 31% (45/147) in control cells (Figure 3L,M).
evidence: Quantification of cell division orientation from in utero electroporation experiments analyzing 137 SPAG5 knockdown cells and 147 control cells (Figure 3L,M).

claim: SPAG5 knockdown causes a bias toward non-planar divisions in electroporated aNPCs.
source: There is a bias toward non-planar divisions (larger angles) in sh-SPAG5-electroporated aNPCs when compared with scrambled shRNA, p=0.0009.
evidence: Statistical analysis of spindle orientation angles from in utero electroporation experiments showing significant shift toward larger angles (Figure 3L).

claim: Around 18% of NSCs are aCas3 positive in Diaph3 cKO mice at E11.5 compared to 2.4% in control.
source: To assess the effect of DIAPH3 loss on cortical neurogenesis, we performed aCas3 immunostaining at E11.5 and found that around 18% of NSCs were aCas3 positive in Diaph3 cKO mice (18 ± 0.83% of cells in Diaph3 cKO versus 2.4 ± 0.65% in control; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Quantification of activated caspase-3 positive cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E11.5 brain sections (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: The number of Pax6+ apical neural progenitor cells decreases by 36% in Diaph3 cKO at E13.5.
source: We quantified the number of aNPCs (Pax6), BP (Tbr2), and neurons (Tbr1) at E13.5, and found that the three populations were affected (Figure 4A–I). Their respective numbers decreased by 36% (number of Pax6+ cells/0.1mm2 = 502 ± 48 in Diaph3 cKO versus 786 ± 35 in control; Figure 4A–C)
evidence: Quantification of Pax6+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E13.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4A-C).

claim: The number of Tbr2+ basal progenitor cells decreases by 31% in Diaph3 cKO at E13.5.
source: 31% (number of Tbr2+ cells/0.1mm2 = 234 ± 4.8 in Diaph3 cKO versus 339 ± 15 in control; Figure 4D–F)
evidence: Quantification of Tbr2+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E13.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4D-F).

claim: The number of Tbr1+ neurons decreases by 23% in Diaph3 cKO at E13.5.
source: and 23% (number of Tbr1+ cells/0.1mm2 = 404 ± 12 in Diaph3 cKO versus 524 ± 18 in controls; Figure 4G–I).
evidence: Quantification of Tbr1+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E13.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4G-I).

claim: In control embryos, 87% of divisions are planar and 13% are non-planar in aNPCs.
source: In control embryos, 87% (77/89) of divisions were planar and 13% (12/89) were non-planar.
evidence: Quantification of cell division orientation from analysis of 89 dividing cells in control embryos (Figure 4K,L).

claim: In Diaph3 cKO, the fraction of planar divisions drops to 46% and non-planar divisions increase to 54%.
source: In Diaph3 cKO, the fraction of planar divisions dropped to 46% (37/81), whereas that of non-planar divisions increased to 54% (44/81) (Figure 4K,L).
evidence: Quantification of cell division orientation from analysis of 81 dividing cells in Diaph3 cKO embryos (Figure 4K,L).

claim: Multipolar spindles are observed in Diaph3 cKO tissue.
source: We also observed signs of multipolar spindles in Diaph3 cKO tissue (Figure 4M,N), a phenotype that is reminiscent of DIAPH3 and SPAG5 knockdown (Figure 1, Figure 3).
evidence: Immunofluorescence images showing multipolar spindles in Diaph3 cKO tissue (Figure 4M,N).

claim: The fraction of proliferating cells (BrdU+Ki67+/BrdU+) is reduced by 15% in Diaph3 cKO at e14.5.
source: The fraction of proliferating cells (BrdU+Ki67+/BrdU+) was reduced (−15%, p=0.011; Figure 4P)
evidence: Quantification of BrdU and Ki67 double-positive cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E14.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4P).

claim: The fraction of precursors which exited the cell cycle (BrdU+Ki67-/BrdU+) is enhanced by 20% in Diaph3 cKO at e14.5.
source: whereas that of precursors which exited the cell cycle (BrdU+Ki67-/BrdU+) was enhanced in Diaph3 cKO compared with controls (+20%, p=0.011; Figure 4Q).
evidence: Quantification of BrdU+Ki67- cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E14.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4Q).

claim: The ratio of non-cycling to cycling cells (BrdU+Ki67-/BrdU+Ki67+) is increased by 40% in Diaph3 cKO at e14.5.
source: Accordingly, the ratio of non-cycling to cycling cells (BrdU+Ki67-/BrdU+Ki67+) was increased in Diaph3 cKO (+40%, p=0.0078; Figure 4R)
evidence: Quantification of the ratio of BrdU+Ki67- to BrdU+Ki67+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E14.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4R).

claim: The fraction of cells that underwent neurogenic division (BrdU+Tbr1+/BrdU+) is increased by 15% in Diaph3 cKO at e14.5.
source: and so was the fraction of cells that underwent neurogenic division (BrdU+Tbr1+/BrdU+: +15%, p=0.0031; Figure 4—figure supplement 1S).
evidence: Quantification of BrdU+Tbr1+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of E14.5 brain sections from three embryos per genotype (Figure 4—figure supplement 1S).

claim: The cerebral cortex of adult Diaph3 cKO mice is markedly thin.
source: The cerebral cortex of adult Diaph3 cKO mice was markedly thin (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: Dark field micrographs showing reduced cortical thickness in adult Diaph3 cKO mice (Figure 5A,B).

claim: Cortex thickness is reduced from 1.5 ± 0.014 mm in control to 1.3 ± 0.028 mm in Diaph3 cKO adult mice.
source: (1.3 ± 0.028 mm in Diaph3 cKO versus 1.5 ± 0.014 mm in control, p=0.00038).
evidence: Quantification of cortical thickness from brain sections of four mice per genotype (Figure 5B).

claim: The number of Cux1+ cells in layers II-III is reduced from 933 ± 73 in control to 614 ± 20 in Diaph3 cKO.
source: (D) Quantification of the number of Cux1+ cells (left) and thickness (right) in layers II-III (Cux1+ cells: 614 ± 20 cells in Diaph3 cKO versus 933 ± 73 in control, p=0.0056; thickness: 385 ± 15 μm in Diaph3 cKO versus 482 ± 13 μm in control, p=0.0025).
evidence: Quantification of Cux1+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of adult brain sections from four mice per genotype (Figure 5C,D).

claim: The thickness of layers II-III is reduced from 482 ± 13 μm in control to 385 ± 15 μm in Diaph3 cKO.
source: (D) Quantification of the number of Cux1+ cells (left) and thickness (right) in layers II-III (Cux1+ cells: 614 ± 20 cells in Diaph3 cKO versus 933 ± 73 in control, p=0.0056; thickness: 385 ± 15 μm in Diaph3 cKO versus 482 ± 13 μm in control, p=0.0025).
evidence: Quantification of layer thickness from immunofluorescence analysis of adult brain sections from four mice per genotype (Figure 5C,D).

claim: The number of Foxp2+ cells in layer VI is reduced from 558 ± 32 in control to 375 ± 22 in Diaph3 cKO.
source: (F) Quantification of the number of Foxp2+ cells (left) and thickness (right) in layer VI (Foxp2+ cells: 375 ± 22 cells in Diaph3 cKO versus 558 ± 32 in control, p=0.0033; thickness: 383 ± 20 μm in Diaph3 cKO versus 505 ± 8 μm in control, p=0.0012).
evidence: Quantification of Foxp2+ cells from immunofluorescence analysis of adult brain sections from four mice per genotype (Figure 5E,F).

claim: The thickness of layer VI is reduced from 505 ± 8 μm in control to 383 ± 20 μm in Diaph3 cKO.
source: (F) Quantification of the number of Foxp2+ cells (left) and thickness (right) in layer VI (Foxp2+ cells: 375 ± 22 cells in Diaph3 cKO versus 558 ± 32 in control, p=0.0033; thickness: 383 ± 20 μm in Diaph3 cKO versus 505 ± 8 μm in control, p=0.0012).
evidence: Quantification of layer thickness from immunofluorescence analysis of adult brain sections from four mice per genotype (Figure 5E,F).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice display lower spontaneous locomotor activity in open-field test.
source: Diaph3 cKO mice displayed lower spontaneous locomotor activity in open-field test and elevated plus maze (Figure 5G,H)
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing reduced distance moved in open field test (Figure 5G).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice display lower spontaneous locomotor activity in elevated plus maze.
source: Diaph3 cKO mice displayed lower spontaneous locomotor activity in open-field test and elevated plus maze (Figure 5G,H)
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing reduced distance travelled in elevated plus maze (Figure 5H).

claim: DIAPH3 deficiency has little effect on anxiety and/or attention as measured by time spent in periphery of open field or closed arms of elevated plus maze.
source: but no difference was detected when we analyzed the time spent in the periphery of the open field or in the closed arms of the elevated plus maze (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B). These results suggest that DIAPH3 deficiency impairs locomotor activity, but has little effect, if any, on anxiety and/or attention.
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing no significant difference in anxiety-related measures (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice spend more time in the empty chamber than with a stranger mouse in the three-chamber test.
source: In addition, Diaph3 cKO mice exhibited a defective social behavior in the 'three-chamber' test. They spent more time in the empty chamber than with a stranger mouse (stranger 1), emphasizing the lower sociability of Diaph3 cKO mice, as compared to control littermates (Figure 5I).
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing impaired social preference in three-chamber test (Figure 5I).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice spend less time with a new stranger mouse in the social novelty test.
source: When another stranger mouse was introduced, Diaph3 cKO mice spent less time with the new stranger, indicating impairment in social novelty behavior (Figure 5J).
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing impaired social novelty behavior in three-chamber test (Figure 5J).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice do not show any olfactory defect.
source: Diaph3 cKO mice did not show any olfactory defect (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing no significant difference in food localization test (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice perform as well as controls in the Morris water maze test.
source: They performed as well as controls in the Morris water maze (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D) and modified Y-maze tests (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), implying that long-term and short-term memories were preserved.
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing no significant difference in Morris water maze test (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice perform as well as controls in the modified Y-maze test.
source: They performed as well as controls in the Morris water maze (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D) and modified Y-maze tests (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), implying that long-term and short-term memories were preserved.
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing no significant difference in modified Y-maze test (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).

claim: Long-term and short-term memories are preserved in Diaph3 cKO mice.
source: They performed as well as controls in the Morris water maze (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D) and modified Y-maze tests (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), implying that long-term and short-term memories were preserved.
evidence: Behavioral testing data showing normal performance in memory tests (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice do not display repetitive behavior as assayed by self-grooming.
source: Finally, they did not display any repetitive behavior, as assayed by self-grooming (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F) or marble burying (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing no significant difference in self-grooming test (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).

claim: Diaph3 cKO mice do not display repetitive behavior as assayed by marble burying.
source: Finally, they did not display any repetitive behavior, as assayed by self-grooming (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F) or marble burying (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Behavioral testing data from 10 mice per genotype showing no significant difference in marble burying test (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).

claim: DIAPH3 is required for cytokinesis as its dysfunction impairs the contractile ring and produces multinucleated cells.
source: DIAPH3 is essential for cytokinesis as its dysfunction impairs the contractile ring and produces multinucleated cells.
evidence: Statement in the abstract summarizing established knowledge about DIAPH3 function.

claim: DIAPH3 regulates the assembly and bipolarity of the mitotic spindle.
source: Here, we report that DIAPH3 localizes at the centrosome during mitosis and regulates the assembly and bipolarity of the mitotic spindle.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: DIAPH3-deficient cells display disorganized cytoskeleton and multipolar spindles.
source: DIAPH3-deficient cells display disorganized cytoskeleton and multipolar spindles.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: DIAPH3 deficiency disrupts the expression and/or stability of several proteins including SPAG5.
source: DIAPH3 deficiency disrupts the expression and/or stability of several proteins including the kinetochore-associated protein SPAG5.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: DIAPH3 and SPAG5 have similar expression patterns in the developing brain.
source: DIAPH3 and SPAG5 have similar expression patterns in the developing brain and overlapping subcellular localization during mitosis.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on expression data and immunofluorescence findings.

claim: DIAPH3 and SPAG5 have overlapping subcellular localization during mitosis.
source: DIAPH3 and SPAG5 have similar expression patterns in the developing brain and overlapping subcellular localization during mitosis.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on immunofluorescence findings showing both proteins at centrosomes.

claim: Knockdown of SPAG5 phenocopies DIAPH3 deficiency.
source: Knockdown of SPAG5 phenocopies DIAPH3 deficiency, whereas its overexpression rescues the DIAHP3 knockdown phenotype.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on experimental findings showing similar phenotypes and rescue experiments.

claim: Overexpression of SPAG5 rescues the DIAPH3 knockdown phenotype.
source: Knockdown of SPAG5 phenocopies DIAPH3 deficiency, whereas its overexpression rescues the DIAHP3 knockdown phenotype.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on rescue experiments showing restoration of cell viability and spindle bipolarity.

claim: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex profoundly disrupts neurogenesis.
source: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex profoundly disrupts neurogenesis, depleting cortical progenitors and neurons, leading to cortical malformation and autistic-like behavior.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on in vivo experiments in Diaph3 cKO mice.

claim: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex depletes cortical progenitors and neurons.
source: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex profoundly disrupts neurogenesis, depleting cortical progenitors and neurons, leading to cortical malformation and autistic-like behavior.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on quantification of different cell populations in Diaph3 cKO mice.

claim: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex leads to cortical malformation.
source: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex profoundly disrupts neurogenesis, depleting cortical progenitors and neurons, leading to cortical malformation and autistic-like behavior.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on anatomical analysis of adult Diaph3 cKO mice showing reduced cortical thickness.

claim: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex leads to autistic-like behavior.
source: Conditional inactivation of Diaph3 in mouse cerebral cortex profoundly disrupts neurogenesis, depleting cortical progenitors and neurons, leading to cortical malformation and autistic-like behavior.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract based on behavioral testing showing impaired locomotor activity and social interactions.

claim: DIAPH3 belongs to a molecular toolbox that links microtubule dynamics during mitosis to aneuploidy, cell death, fate determination defects, and cortical malformation.
source: Our data uncover the uncharacterized functions of DIAPH3 and provide evidence that this protein belongs to a molecular toolbox that links microtubule dynamics during mitosis to aneuploidy, cell death, fate determination defects, and cortical malformation.
evidence: Summary statement in the abstract integrating multiple experimental findings into a broader functional framework.

claim: DIAPH3 is a member of the formin proteins that have the capacity to nucleate and elongate actin filaments.
source: Diaphanous (DIAPH) three (DIAPH3) is a member of the formin proteins that have the capacity to nucleate and elongate actin filaments and, therefore, to remodel the cytoskeleton.
evidence: Statement in the abstract describing established knowledge about DIAPH3 protein family.

claim: DIAPH3 has the capacity to remodel the cytoskeleton.
source: Diaphanous (DIAPH) three (DIAPH3) is a member of the formin proteins that have the capacity to nucleate and elongate actin filaments and, therefore, to remodel the cytoskeleton.
evidence: Statement in the abstract describing established knowledge about DIAPH3 function based on its actin-related activities.

claim: SPAG5 is a kinetochore-associated protein.
source: DIAPH3 deficiency disrupts the expression and/or stability of several proteins including the kinetochore-associated protein SPAG5.
evidence: Statement in the abstract describing the known localization of SPAG5.

claim: Previous studies have associated DIAPH3 mutations with autism spectrum disorder in humans.
source: These results show that Diaph3 cKO mice have specific deficits in motor activity and social behavior, which is in line with previous studies that have associated DIAPH3 mutations with autism spectrum disorder in humans (Vorstman et al., 2011; Xie et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing previous clinical studies linking DIAPH3 to autism spectrum disorder.

claim: DIAPH3 is involved in filopodia assembly, supporting cell migration.
source: DIAPH3 is also involved in filopodia assembly, supporting cell migration (Stastna et al., 2012), and mesenchymal-amoeboid transition (Hager et al., 2012; Morley et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies on DIAPH3 function in cell migration.

claim: DIAPH3 is involved in mesenchymal-amoeboid transition.
source: DIAPH3 is also involved in filopodia assembly, supporting cell migration (Stastna et al., 2012), and mesenchymal-amoeboid transition (Hager et al., 2012; Morley et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies on DIAPH3 function in cell transition.

claim: Early in vitro studies have suggested that DIAPH3 interacts with EB1 and APC, which localizes to plus-end, thereby stabilizing MT.
source: Early in vitro studies have suggested that DIAPH3 interacts with EB1 and APC, which localizes to plus-end, thereby stabilizing MT (Wen et al., 2004; Bartolini et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement citing previous in vitro studies on DIAPH3 interaction with microtubule-associated proteins.

claim: Analysis of the full Diaph3 knockout mice has revealed an important role of DIAPH3 in the biology of NSCs.
source: Analysis of the full Diaph3 knockout mice has revealed an important role of DIAPH3 in the biology of NSCs. The lack of DIAPH3 severely compromises chromosome segregation, leading to aneuploidy, mitotic catastrophe, and loss of these cells (Damiani et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing previous study on full Diaph3 knockout mice.

claim: The lack of DIAPH3 severely compromises chromosome segregation, leading to aneuploidy, mitotic catastrophe, and loss of NSCs.
source: The lack of DIAPH3 severely compromises chromosome segregation, leading to aneuploidy, mitotic catastrophe, and loss of these cells (Damiani et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing previous study on full Diaph3 knockout mice.

claim: SPAG5 localizes at the centrosome and kinetochore and has a documented function in cell division.
source: One of the affected proteins is SPAG5 (also known as the mitotic spindle-associated protein 126 or Astrin), which localizes at the centrosome and kinetochore, and has a documented function in cell division.
evidence: Statement describing known properties of SPAG5 based on established literature.

claim: SPAG5 is also known as the mitotic spindle-associated protein 126 or Astrin.
source: One of the affected proteins is SPAG5 (also known as the mitotic spindle-associated protein 126 or Astrin), which localizes at the centrosome and kinetochore, and has a documented function in cell division.
evidence: Statement providing alternative nomenclature for SPAG5.

claim: SPAG5 is essential to the recruitment of other centrosomal proteins such as CDK5RAP2 (MCPH3).
source: Among those, SPAG5, which localizes at the centrosome and kinetochore, is essential to the recruitment of other centrosomal proteins such as CDK5RAP2 (MCPH3) (Kodani et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement citing previous study on SPAG5 function in recruiting centrosomal proteins.

claim: SPAG5 controls sister chromatid cohesion by regulating separase activity.
source: SPAG5 controls sister chromatid cohesion by regulating separase activity (Thein et al., 2007).
evidence: Statement citing previous study on SPAG5 function in chromosome segregation.

claim: Knockdown of SPAG5 induces similar mitotic errors to those triggered by knockdown of DIAPH3.
source: Knockdown of SPAG5 induces similar mitotic errors to those triggered by knockdown of DIAPH3 (Kodani et al., 2015; Thein et al., 2007 and this work)
evidence: Statement integrating findings from previous studies and current work showing similar phenotypes.

claim: DIAPH3 may serve as a scaffold protein that binds to and stabilizes MT.
source: These results are consistent with previous in vitro data, suggesting that DIAPH3 may serve as a scaffold protein that binds to and stabilizes MT (Palazzo et al., 2001; Bartolini et al., 2008; Wen et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement citing previous in vitro studies and integrating them with current findings.

claim: DIAPH3 sits at the heart of cell division accuracy and fate determination by regulating centrosome integrity, microtubule stability, and spindle orientation.
source: By regulating centrosome integrity, microtubule stability, and spindle orientation, DIAPH3 sits at the heart of cell division accuracy and fate determination (Figure 6).
evidence: Summary statement integrating multiple experimental findings into a functional model.

claim: The centrosome acts as a seed and anchoring point for the minus end of MT as they grow toward the equatorial region (spindle MT) or the cell cortex (astral MT).
source: The centrosome acts as a seed and anchoring point for the minus end of MT as they grow toward the equatorial region (spindle MT) or the cell cortex (astral MT).
evidence: Statement describing established knowledge about centrosome function in mitosis.

claim: Depletion of DIAPH3 disrupts the centrosome and results in disorganized spindle and astral MT, abnormal alignment, and segregation of chromosomes.
source: Consistent with this, we found that depletion of DIAPH3 disrupts the centrosome and results in disorganized spindle and astral MT, abnormal alignment, and segregation of chromosomes.
evidence: Summary statement integrating multiple experimental observations from the study.

claim: Primary microcephaly is an inherited neurodevelopmental defect that appears mostly during pregnancy or at the first postnatal year.
source: Primary microcephaly is an inherited neurodevelopmental defect that appears mostly during pregnancy or at the first postnatal year.
evidence: Statement describing established clinical knowledge about primary microcephaly.

claim: Eighteen 'microcephaly' genes named MCPH 1–18 have been identified.
source: Eighteen 'microcephaly' genes named MCPH 1–18 (for microcephaly primary hereditary 1–18) have been identified (Jayaraman et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement citing previous review on microcephaly genes.

claim: All microcephaly genes are expressed in the germinal zones, wherein the neural progenitors reside, proliferate, and differentiate into neurons during the second trimester of pregnancy.
source: All these genes are expressed in the germinal zones, wherein the neural progenitors reside, proliferate, and differentiate into neurons during the second trimester of pregnancy (Verloes et al., 1993; Gilmore and Walsh, 2013).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies on microcephaly gene expression patterns.

claim: Loss of function of DIAPH3 disrupts the modality of cell division and fate determination of apical progenitors, enhancing the number of neurogenic divisions at the expense of proliferative division.
source: Loss of function of DIAPH3 disrupts the modality of cell division and fate determination of apical progenitors, enhancing the number of neurogenic divisions at the expense of proliferative division, prematurely exhausting the pool of progenitors.
evidence: Summary statement integrating findings on cell division orientation and cell fate from BrdU experiments.

claim: Loss of function of DIAPH3 prematurely exhausts the pool of progenitors.
source: Loss of function of DIAPH3 disrupts the modality of cell division and fate determination of apical progenitors, enhancing the number of neurogenic divisions at the expense of proliferative division, prematurely exhausting the pool of progenitors.
evidence: Summary statement integrating findings on reduced progenitor numbers and increased neurogenic divisions.

claim: The loss of GPSM2 does not lead to microcephaly despite the randomized cleavage planes in dividing neural progenitors.
source: Even though the cytocortical proteins help to orientate the mitotic spindle, the loss of GPSM2 does not lead to microcephaly despite the randomized cleavage planes in dividing neural progenitors (Konno et al., 2008; Blumer et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies on GPSM2 knockout mice.

claim: The role of DIAPH3 in fidelity of nuclear division and the cell loss observed in Diaph3 cKO mice may be more instrumental to the emergence of microcephaly than its role in oriented cell division.
source: Therefore, the role of DIAPH3 in fidelity of nuclear division and the cell loss observed in Diaph3 cKO mice may be more instrumental to the emergence of microcephaly in Diaph3 cKO mice than its role in oriented cell division.
evidence: Interpretive statement based on comparison with GPSM2 knockout phenotype and integration of multiple findings.

claim: Patients with microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type 1 (MOPD 1) syndrome display a 50% reduction in DIAPH3 expression.
source: In support of this, patients with microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type 1 (MOPD 1) syndrome display a 50% reduction in DIAPH3 expression (Edery et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement citing previous clinical study on DIAPH3 expression in MOPD1 patients.

claim: The Diaph3 gene has been associated with body size in equines, as copy number variants were reported in donkeys, ponies, and horses with short stature.
source: Furthermore, the Diaph3 gene has been associated with body size in equines, as copy number variants were reported in donkeys, ponies, and horses with short stature (Metzger et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement citing previous study on Diaph3 genetic variants in equines.

claim: Two clinical studies point to DIAPH3 as an autism susceptibility gene.
source: In humans, two clinical studies point to DIAPH3 as an autism susceptibility gene (Vorstman et al., 2011; Xie et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing two previous clinical studies linking DIAPH3 to autism.

claim: A double-hit mutation in DIAPH3 with one amino acid substitution (Pro614Thr) in one allele and a deletion in the second allele has been identified in autism patients.
source: The first study identified a double-hit mutation with one amino acid substitution (Pro614Thr) in one allele and a deletion in the second allele.
evidence: Statement describing findings from a previous clinical study on DIAPH3 mutations in autism.

claim: A de novo point mutation in the 18th exon of DIAPH3 (c.2156T > C, pI719T) has been identified in autism patients.
source: The second is a de novo point mutation in the 18th exon (c.2156T > C, pI719T).
evidence: Statement describing findings from a previous clinical study on DIAPH3 mutations in autism.

claim: Several chromosomal deletions spanning the DIAPH3 locus have been associated with language impairment, autism, and intellectual disability.
source: Several chromosomal deletions spanning the DIAPH3 locus have also been associated with language impairment, autism, and intellectual disability (https://decipher.sanger.ac.uk/ and Nathalie Sans et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing database and previous study on chromosomal deletions involving DIAPH3.

claim: Among autistic patients, a significant fraction exhibits microcephaly.
source: Importantly, among autistic patients, a significant fraction exhibits microcephaly (Fombonne et al., 1999).
evidence: Statement citing previous clinical study on the prevalence of microcephaly in autism.

claim: The deletion of Diaph3 affects the accuracy and modalities of division of neural progenitor cells, ultimately regulating the final number of cortical neurons.
source: Our finding that the deletion of Diaph3 affects the accuracy and modalities of division of neural progenitor cells, ultimately regulating the final number of cortical neurons, may provide a molecular and cellular basis to the brain malformations and neurological disorders that have been associated with DIAPH3 dysfunction in humans.
evidence: Summary statement integrating multiple experimental findings from the study.

claim: DIAPH3 deficiency induces centrosome abnormalities and disrupts spindle and astral MT.
source: Combined together, our results suggest a novel role of DIAPH3 as a centrosomal protein. Its deficiency induces centrosome abnormalities and disrupts spindle and astral MT.
evidence: Summary statement integrating multiple experimental findings from the study.

claim: DIAPH3 deficiency causes inaccuracies in nuclear division and fate decision of neural progenitors, leading to the loss of cortical progenitors, microcephaly, and autistic-like behavior.
source: These defects cause inaccuracies in nuclear division and fate decision of neural progenitors, leading to the loss of cortical progenitors, microcephaly, and autistic-like behavior.
evidence: Summary statement integrating multiple experimental findings from the study into a causal chain.
